Synopsis:
    The US and Iran have entered a new cycle of military exchange, with US airstrikes on Iranian targets prompting Iranian ballistic missile and drone counterstrikes across Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq. Iran has tightened its effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz to oil shipping, threatening to block all Gulf oil exports if pressure continues. Oil prices are already rising. Diplomatic efforts via a June MOU have broken down. Both sides are issuing escalatory rhetoric with no de-escalation signals visible.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — content is about US-Iran military escalation and its impact on oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz; no direct reference to EU/German energy markets

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 72 — a US-Iran military flare-up was a known tail risk, but the scale of bilateral strikes, the active Hormuz closure, and explicit Iranian threats to block all Gulf oil exports represent a meaningful escalation beyond baseline expectations
